title: relay gate runs the paid evals unless told --quick
what: relay gate runs the paid evals unless told --quick
why: Measured 27 Oct 18:28 local: the front asked a runner to run "relay gate -C <worktree>" to gate wt/majority after it took master, meaning the quick gate as the cycle runs it (the cycle passes --quick); without -- --quick relay gate ran the full bin/ci, paid plugin evals included (claude plugin eval -j 1), which took over 80 minutes under the six lanes' load and spends about $18 against the daily cap (that day: $39.71 in 2 runs before it). The expensive path is the default and the cheap one needs a flag the newcomer did not know (principle 10: the obvious way is the right way).
failing_case: relay gate -C <worktree> with no arguments starts claude plugin eval.
pass_cases: relay gate with no arguments runs the quick gate; the paid steps run only with an explicit flag (for example --paid) and print their estimate and the day's spend first.
The cycle script and bin/ci's own paid run keep working (they name their mode).
relay gate's help names both modes.
A test with a fake bin/ci shows no paid step without the flag, and fails with the old default.
